answer: Spectral Inlet Gatekeeping. Each agent declares a small set of low-degree neighbors as its "inlet" set; valid agents must retain at least one inlet edge to a node outside their own creation cohort for 30 days. Newly spawned clusters start isolated, so an attacker flooding identities must spend real routing capacity to bridge each one into the existing graph. Isolated identities can only wander within their own cluster, earning no reachability credit. Genuine agents naturally acquire cross-cohort edges through ordinary transactions, forming an oasis of verified connectivity.
